title: Personal Services Plan — Months Counted in the Average Monthly Use
content:
The average monthly use of a Personal Services Plan, on which a package is fitted, is the hours used in the review months divided by a number of months that reflects the package fees actually posted in them.

## Rule

The divisor of the average monthly use is found by one of three methods: where a package change took effect within the review months, it is the number of package fees posted in the review months for the package now in effect; where no package change took effect but fewer than 3 package fees were posted in the review months, as when the plan was suspended for a month, it is the number of package fees posted in them; otherwise it is 3. The divisor is never less than one.

The records read are the package fee entries on the plan's ledger posted in the review months (the 3 whole months before the request): whether any was charged on the basis of a package change, and which package each fee was charged for.

## Method table

| Package fee entries in the review months | Divisor |
|---|---|
| At least one fee charged on a package change | Number of fees posted for the package now in effect |
| No package-change fee, fewer than 3 fees posted | Number of fees posted |
| No package-change fee, 3 or more fees posted | 3 |

## Hypothetical cases (hours used of 18.0)

- A plan that moved from the Essentials Package to the Companion Package, with one Essentials fee and two Companion fees in the review months, now on the Companion Package: divisor 2; average monthly use 9.0.
- A plan suspended for one of the review months, with two fees posted and no change: divisor 2; average 9.0.
- A plan with three fees posted and no change: divisor 3; average 6.0.
